01. Each open position has specific attachment requirements in order to be considered by the hiring committee. If the attachment directions are not followed, your application will not be considered. The required attachments for this position are: • Cover letter (see instructions in Additional Information section); • Resume; • Professional Reference List (see instructions in Additional Information section); • Unofficial Transcripts. (See further document instructions below); Have you attached the correct required documents to your application? Options: Yes | No
Perform work from elevated positions such as ladders and motorized lifts (when necessary and once licensed);
Associate’s degree and two years of work experience or a combination of education and experience which would indicate possession of the knowledge, skills and abilities listed.
Associate’s degree and two years of work experience in computer and networking technology or related field.
Installation, support, and maintenance of college hardware, software, audiovisual, VoIP, and unified communications;
Install, program, maintain, and deploy videoconferencing and audiovisual systems, including low voltage cabling;
Diagnose and repair or facilitate repairs of non-functioning computing, audiovisual, VoIP, and unified communications equipment;
Provide in-classroom repairs and instructional emergency service for supported equipment;
Design, implement, and keep system standards up to date for various configurations throughout the district;
Troubleshoot connectivity issues and take appropriate steps to repair and/or facilitate appropriate escalation of support where/when necessary;
Receive, screen and follow through on user requests with established guidelines and priorities;
Research, evaluate and recommend hardware, software and operating systems in support of campus standards;
Assist users in selection of equipment that best meets their needs in keeping with campus standards;
Maintain accurate equipment and parts inventory;
Maintain department standards and follow established procedures;
Attend trainings, meetings and workshops where/when identified;

Utilize, design and document automation of processes for provisioning, deployment, updating and maintaining security of networked computers, peripherals, audiovisual, mobile devices, VoIP equipment, and unified communications equipment;
Monitor and review compliance with software license agreements;
Research, specify, configure, utilize and maintain related client/server asset management/monitoring and remote-control systems;

In coordination with network and other IT staff, specify, configure, automate, provisions, troubleshoot, and update resources critical to the functioning services provided by the Information Technology department; and
Perform other related duties as required.
Tools, materials and equipment used in repair and maintenance of computer equipment;
Adapt to new technology.
Computer hardware components and related peripherals;
Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with those contacted in the performance of duties. and
Microsoft, Apple, and Google operating systems and applications;

Demonstrate a sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, and ethnic backgrounds of staff and students and of staff and students with physical and learning disabilities.
Audiovisual and control systems commonly used in a variety of settings (classroom, conference room, theater, digital signage, etc.);
Read and comprehend printed matter and text and data on computer monitors;
Wiring schematics for electronic systems; blueprints when used for technology related systems;
Sit or stand for extended periods of time;
VoIP and unified communications related hardware and software:
Lift and/or carry 50 pounds; and
Basic network troubleshooting and diagnostic utilities, such as ip/ifconfig, ping, gpresult and packet sniffing;
Exert manual dexterity sufficient for keyboard and other office equipment operation.
Basic understanding of common network protocols such as TCP/IP, PXE, TFTP, HTTP(S), FTP, SIP, IMAP, SMTP and SSH;
Wireless configuration, low voltage cabling and patching in network ports;
Endpoint security software including anti-malware and anti-virus;

Processes for managing, provisioning, deployment, and inventory management of computers, software and mobile devices, utilizing such platforms as Microsoft Active Directory, Microsoft SCCM, Jamf Pro, Apple Configurator, and Google Admin Console;
Install, configure, and troubleshoot networked computer workstations, systems and programs, and VoIP endpoints used by the district in both instruction and administrative areas;
Current technologies, personal computer, and associated office software such as word processing, spreadsheet, presentation, and/or database software;
Correct usage of English, grammar, spelling, punctuation, and vocabulary; and
District policies and procedures.
Communicate intelligibly and effectively via speech, telephone, written correspondence, and/or email;
